headline: Recovery week is underway — the two lightest days of the block follow the long run, with easy-run HR sitting well below the prior period.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Coming off the closed four-week block, you've stepped into a lighter phase with the two most recent runs — the moderate 12 km and the long 21 km — bracketing the load without adding much on top. This reads as intentional consolidation rather than a dip in preparedness, especially with volume still up on the prior block and strength frequency holding at double the earlier rate. Nothing here suggests fatigue accumulating faster than you can absorb it; the strain-to-tolerance balance remains in productive territory.

The aerobic-efficiency signal you've been building continues to be the through-line: comparable-effort easy runs are landing meaningfully lower on heart rate than the prior period. That's the kind of within-athlete shift that matters more than any single session, and it's held steady enough now to treat as a real base adaptation rather than noise. With St. Olavsleden roughly four weeks out, the general endurance base looks in good shape.

Where the gap remains is specificity: the ascent per run is still modest and rolling, and there's no sign yet of pack-loaded work. The base is ready to carry that specific demand — it just hasn't been asked to yet.
watch_items: Whether weighted-pack running finally enters the schedule, since the aerobic base looks ready but the 6-8kg carry demand is still untrained.
Whether ascent per run begins trending toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.
Whether the sharp sleep swings settle or start clustering short as the event nears — worth noting the recent short night after the long-run day.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 156 km vs 126 km prior block (+24%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 144 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 8 runs)
▬ Strain:tolerance ratio 1.09 (PRODUCTIVE) (strain 94, tolerance 87); sleep averaging 7h36m over the same period
